stories.title: “Wasn’t Jesus Woke?”
stories.text: Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, greets Jerilynn Henrikson on August 20, 2026 at Gravel City Roasters in Emporia, Ks. Henrikson said she is a lifelong Democrat and said, “I know I don’t want Marshall.” Photo: Clayton Steward Story by Clayton Steward and Justin Perkins Adam Hamilton, pastor and founder of Church of the Resurrection in the Kansas City suburbs, the largest United Methodist congregation in the United States, walked into a coffee shop in Emporia, Kansas, in late August. With a population of 24,000, Emporia is roughly the same size as Resurrection’s membership. But instead of preaching, Hamilton was there to make his case for why he can flip a seat for the U.S. Senate from the Sunflower State, a feat more than 90 years in the making. Hamilton told the crowd of about 40 people his campaign is rooted in his faith and experiences as a pastor but clarified that he is not running to force people to be Christian or United Methodist. Instead, he is motivated to uphold the U.S. Constitution and fight for individual rights. stories.text: This is Lever Weekly , a recap of our work from the past week. If you only read one email from us all week, this should be it. The Lever holds the powerful accountable through reader-supported investigative journalism that corporate media will not undertake. Join our mission , and you’ll get great perks in return. Join The Fight Here’s what The Lever published this week: LEVER DEEP DIVE OF THE WEEK AI Regulation Was Coming. Then Trump Killed It. After a flood of tech industry cash, President Donald Trump killed a requirement that AI giants disclose their riskiest experiments to national security officials. Now lawmakers are scrambling to catch up. The Machines Escaped. Their Masters Did So First. The most frightening thing about rogue AI agents may be how faithfully they mirror the powerful humans who created them. LEVER SCOOPS OF THE WEEK The Fine Print In Democrats’ Hollywood Merger Surrender. Democrats promised to play hardball, then accepted loophole-ridden pledges leaving Paramount’s $111 billion megamerger intact. The Ellisons Have Made This Movie Before.
